Placer Supervisors Vote To Continue Marijuana Suppression

Exclusive to MarijuanaNews.com

By J. B. Waters

AUBURN, CA.

Placer County supervisors voted unanimously to approve a resolution authorizing Sheriff Ed Bonner to ask the Office of Criminal Justice Planning for a $206,000 Marijuana Suppression Program grant.

The resolution was passed, without discussion, despite last week’s terrifying pot raid of two innocent elderly people, a $25 million med pot lawsuit, and an angry editorial in the local paper.

See
How Much More Will Bad law Enforcement Cost the Taxpayers of California?
Learning to Take Human Rights Seriously
– Or Why Dehumanizing People Is An Expensive Delusion

Last week, former gubernatorial candidate, Steve Kubby wrote the Board of Supervisors asking them to investigate human rights violations in and around Placer County. Kubby alleged that dozens of legally qualified patients are being raided, humiliated, arrested, looted and pressured into plea bargains. The Placer County Board of Supervisors, has refused to respond to the letter even though it was the subject of a front page story in the local paper. The fact that they have ignored the sheriff's behavior puts the County at greater risk of punitive damages.
See
Kubby Appeals To County Supervisors To Supervise Law Enforcement.

The grant, which has been awarded in previous years, will provide funding for one deputy sheriff, overtime for five more deputies and a sergeant, and a 15 percent portion of costs for a deputy district attorney.

Placer County’s Marijuana Eradication Team implements the grant and related program. No cash match is required from the county.

The department uses state and federal grants to search out illegal marijuana growing operations in the county. Since 1996, it has been using its own fleet of helicopters and planes to augment ground searches.
